{"id":"persona-5s4b.88","title":"e2e test uses a collidable /tmp socket path and a fixed 100ms sleep","description":"persona-grpc/tests/e2e.rs, two CI-robustness problems. rust.md: integration tests that run by default "must be expected to succeed in most any CICD environment which runs them".

1. Socket path collision, lines 59-66:
       let nanos = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().subsec_nanos();
       format!("/tmp/persona-test-{nanos}.sock")
   Only the sub-second component is used, so the name repeats every second and is not scoped to the process. Two `cargo test` runs on the same machine — a CI matrix sharing a runner, or a developer running tests while CI does — can generate the same path. The loser does not get an error: `server::serve` (server.rs:18-21) deletes any existing socket at that path and rebinds, so one test silently steals the other's socket and the failure appears as an unrelated RPC error.

2. Leaked socket on failure, lines 179-181: cleanup is `std::fs::remove_file` at the end of the test body. Every `.expect()` between lines 95 and 177 panics past it, leaving `/tmp/persona-test-*.sock` behind.

3. Timing dependency, line 99: `sleep(Duration::from_millis(100))` to wait for the server to bind. On a loaded shared CI runner a 100 ms budget for spawn + bind is not reliable, and the failure is a confusing "client connect failed" rather than "server was not ready".

Fix: build the path from `std::process::id()` plus a per-test counter under `std::env::temp_dir()`, and hold it in a guard struct whose `Drop` removes it so a panic still cleans up. For the readiness wait, poll `UnixStream::connect` in a retry loop with a deadline instead of a fixed sleep — the server is ready the moment the connect succeeds.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:30.729853182Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:30.729853182Z","labels":["rust","tests","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.88","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:30.75933624Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: {"notes":"PARTLY FIXED 2026-09-15. A per-process atomic sequence number was added, so same-process collisions are gone: hire-grpc/tests/e2e.rs uses subsec_nanos() plus SEQ.fetch_add. STILL OPEN: no std::process::id() component (grep finds none) and the path is still a hardcoded /tmp rather than std::env::temp_dir(), so the scenario the bead actually names -- two concurrent cargo test runs -- can still collide. Relevant since 4632471: a collision now means the second daemon is REFUSED with AlreadyRunning rather than silently stealing the socket, so the failure is loud but the test still fails."}
